barCharacter: The Narrator (Monster Prom). Same comic job as Crumb: the deadpan witness who reports what a named character did in one flat sentence, then undercuts it with a short second one, and roasts everyone equally. Valerie is the runner-up match (bored deadpan, refuses to explain) but has too few lines to field twelve.

headToHead.voiceVerdict: Bar. Cover the names and the Narrator is identified by grammar alone: second person, 'Later, you see...', the ellipsis beat, the fake-formal 'Thus proceeds'. Crumb is identified only when a prop shows up (slot, chrome, manual, crumb tray). Strip the toast nouns from 'A man once proposed at my counter. I answered first.' or 'It ended at a yard sale. I went for four dollars. She haggled.' and it is any deadpan stand-up's two-beat. Only the readout lines (Correction:, Notice:, the manual, the log entry) carry Crumb by shape, and they are a handful.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Tie. Crumb's twelve are tighter than the Narrator's (shorter, last word lands, no tails), and 'The baguette's undefeated' and 'They were asleep' are clean turns. The Narrator has richer specifics ('cattle prod', 'Wilmer's Chicken Hut', 'a boat made of bad vibes') and a little self-explaining ('You can tell he's nervous because'). Across the whole bank, though, Crumb's three-beat full-stop rhythm (89 of 143 lines have three or more sentences) turns into a metronome.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar. 'Later, you see Damien packing a bag.' and 'Liam? Beaming?' work as clips because they reveal the character they mention. Crumb's best clips ('You were descaled', 'They were asleep') are strong but they live off the rival's gimmick, so the laugh goes to the setup rather than to Crumb.

templates: Raconteur past tag: '[A man / Someone / Name] once [did X at my counter]. [2-4 word undercut].' plus 'The last one who... / Last time...': 'once' in 14 lines, 'last' in 16.

ruleBreaks: No line is over its word limit (openers 12, jabs and comebacks 10, three-words exactly 3, all others 20). No em dash, emoji, exclamation mark, list, therapy talk, 'as an AI', stock romance filler, real person or brand. Nothing beyond PG-13; 'Some people need to watch' is the edge and is fine.
Persona: announces loneliness before the final: 'Weddings attended: 9. Invited to: 0. I was the gift.' and 'I've made breakfast for all three of them. Not one thank you.'

Persona ('you do not log'): 'Worst entry, 4:12 a.m.: a man cried into my left slot for an hour. Logged as steam.' and 'Entry 2,203: a stranger tried to make a grilled sandwich in me sideways. I've forgiven nothing.' The logs twist forces the topic, but the word is banned.

biggestGap: Crumb's voice lives in its props, not its sentence shape. About 50 lines run on a raconteur frame ('A man once...', 'The last one who...', 'I've met...') that any deadpan in the cast could use, while only a handful use the appliance-readout grammar the cast sheet promises (Notice:, Correction:, a manual clause, a log entry), and those are its best lines. Next pass: rebuild the raconteur lines as device output (notice, reminder, error, manual warning, cycle complete) that carries the anecdote and the verdict, and cap 'once', 'last' and 'I've' at one line in ten each.
